source.title: Pseudo Relevance Feedback is Enough to Close the Gap Between Small and Large Dense Retrieval Models
source.authors: Hang Li; Xiao Wang; B. Koopman; G. Zuccon

record.file_problem: Some equations and figures are flattened in the text extraction, but the paper is readable and includes its main sections and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: It reports dense-retrieval benchmark results for different-sized LLaMA retrievers, bearing narrowly on downstream performance versus model scale in a new setting. It does not test pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: Only the no-PRF TREC DL model-size comparisons are recorded for V6. PromptPRF and PassPRF results concern deliberately added feedback, not naturally arising scale-dependent performance; the paper also does not report held-out language-model loss, power-law fits, or forecasts from smaller runs.
record.test_reason: This is a pseudo-relevance-feedback (PRF) method paper. It takes 'bigger backbones retrieve better' as its motivation and reports its own method against no-PRF baselines. The no-PRF PromptReps baselines at 3B, 8B and 70B are reference points, not a scaling test. The three backbones are different LLaMA releases (3.2, 3, 3.3), not a controlled size sweep. There is no fit or prediction, no pretraining loss, and no analysis of performance versus scale beyond the ordering. The authors cite scaling laws only to say their PRF result departs from scale-only expectations.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude PromptPRF lets small dense retrievers approach, and sometimes exceed, larger no-PRF retrievers at low query-time cost, as an alternative to scaling the backbone. They frame this as departing from scaling-law expectations, but do not test scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates dense retrieval effectiveness across model sizes; it does not use the original scaling-law loss measurements, training sweeps, or fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Retrieval effectiveness varies with PRF depth, feature type, feature-extractor size, and inclusion of rank information; these are not scaling-law fitting choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Zero-shot PromptReps dense-retrieval nDCG@10 rises from 3B to 8B to 70B LLaMA instruct backbones on TREC DL19 (0.3695/0.5062/0.5291) and DL20 (0.3334/0.4381/0.4579). The gains are much smaller from 8B to 70B than from 3B to 8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Zero-shot LLM-based dense retrieval effectiveness increases with backbone size, with diminishing gains at the largest size (uncontrolled model versions, no fit).

record.problems: The scale comparison uses only three LLaMA backbones and two TREC datasets; the models are different LLaMA versions rather than a controlled parameter-only sweep. The reported baseline scale comparisons provide no uncertainty estimates, and the study does not test predictability or pretraining loss.
record.rows_left_out: PromptPRF and PassPRF intervention outcomes, and other retrieval configurations, were left out because they measure feedback-induced retrieval gains rather than performance arising from model scale alone. Additional model-size and feature comparisons appear in Figures 1–5.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or training regimes.
No fitted or predictive relation of downstream performance to scale or loss. Only three uncontrolled backbones are reported, as baselines.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' with a V6 supports label is overgenerous. The size ordering comes from baseline comparison points for the paper's own method, across different LLaMA releases, with no predictive relationship examined. Figures 1–2 (feature-extractor size) concern the PRF intervention, not naturally arising scale effects.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token counts.
No comparison of architecture shapes at fixed parameter count.
No tests across modalities or the listed training regimes.
Tests retrieval effectiveness for three LLaMA backbones on two TREC DL datasets, but not a fitted predictive relationship, pretraining loss, or a broad range of downstream tasks.
No comparison of scaling-law fitting choices, exponents, or curve bending.
